summary: Miraflores is a district of Lima overlooking the Pacific coast. Its waterfront is known for the high Costa Verde cliffs, gardens and the seafront promenade known as the malecón. From here, broad views open up over the ocean and coastal road.

  src: /media/excursions/muzej-larko-staraya-taverna-s-pisko-i-magicheskij-marshrut-vody/gallery-2-enhanced-20261001.webp

The city feels different from its colonial center when viewed from the waterfront. Enclosed squares give way to an open horizon, green slopes and modern buildings. Among the places to stop along the malecón is Parque del Amor, the Park of Love, with its mosaic benches.

Miraflores is worth exploring as a separate part of a visit to Lima. The time available for a walk and the specific stops depend on the itinerary you choose.

At Miralago, the road to Otavalo offers a good reason to stop. Lake San Pablo stretches out before you, with Imbabura rising beyond it. Fields and villages cover the lower slopes; higher up, the greenery gives way to dark volcanic rock. Sometimes clouds hide the summit, then lift to reveal it fully for a few minutes.

This viewpoint lets you take in the whole landscape at once: the water, the shores and the great volcano beyond. Step away from the car, breathe the cool Andean air and linger over the view. For photographs, it is worth waiting until the light falls across the slopes. Even a brief pause reveals how closely rural life and mountains coexist in this part of Ecuador.

Miralago is easy to include on a journey from Quito to the Otavalo market and other places in Imbabura Province. The main reason to come is simple: to look down on San Pablo and let the drive become part of the experience. It is an excellent stop for travelers who love taking home expansive mountain views.
